q: You have one tested image. Test and production need different API addresses. What is the right way?
options: Edit the address in the code and build a new image for production
Keep the same image and give each place its own value as an environment variable when it starts
Keep two Dockerfiles with the addresses written inside
Copy the config file into the image after the build
why: Build once and give each place its own settings from outside the code. Then production runs the same image you tested, and only the setting changes.

q: Is DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:pw@db:5432/shop a setting or a secret?
options: A setting, because its name has no word like password
A setting, because it is only an address
A secret, because the value holds the password
It depends on the log level
why: Use the poster test: if printing the value on a poster would let someone in, it is a secret. The password sits inside the value, even though the name does not say so.

q: You committed .env by mistake, then deleted it in the next commit. Is the secret gone?
options: Yes, the file is no longer in the folder
Yes, git removes deleted files from history
No, the first commit still holds it, so you must change the secret
Only if you also run git push
why: Git remembers every commit. The text is still in the first commit and git show prints it. Treat the secret as public and change it.

q: You build a Next.js image with NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=a and start the container with -e NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=b. What value does the browser code use?
options: b, because the container started last
a, because the value was pasted into the files at build time
Whichever is longer
It asks the server at each page load
why: Next.js inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_ values into the code at build time, so they are frozen in the image. These files are public, so such a name must never hold a secret.

q: A Dockerfile runs COPY .env and then RUN rm .env. Why does the secret still ship with the image?
options: rm does not work in Alpine
A layer only adds. The COPY layer still holds the file, and rm only adds a layer that hides it
Docker keeps a copy of every file in the build folder
Only if the image is public
why: A layer is never changed after it is made. Use a .dockerignore, and RUN --mount=type=secret for a build step that needs a secret. If it already shipped, change the secret.

q: An API key was pushed to a public repo 10 minutes ago. What do you do first?
options: Rewrite the git history and force push
Delete the file in a new commit
Revoke or rotate the key, then check how it was used and clean up
Make the repo private and wait
why: Changing the secret is the only step that stops a copy from working. Rewriting history alone may leave copies elsewhere. Clean up comes after.
